instantiated_cells.justification: Section 86113 requires lobbyist periodic reports within two weeks following the end of each calendar quarter, not annually.
The statute ties the lobbyist's periodic report to the end of each calendar quarter, not a monthly cadence.
Section 86113 sets a quarterly-based reporting cycle, leaving no alternate 'other' frequency specified for lobbyist periodic reports.
A lobbyist must provide the original periodic report to the employer or firm within two weeks following the end of each calendar quarter, indicating quarterly reporting.
Lobbyists' periodic reports are due after each calendar quarter, so the statute does not create a semiannual lobbyist-filed spending report.
The only cadence specified for lobbyist periodic reports is quarterly, not tri-annual or legislative-calendar linked.

A lobbyist's periodic report must include all activity expenses, and when activity expenses are reportable the report must provide date, amount, beneficiary, description, and payee, reflecting itemized expense reporting by lobbyists.
Lobbyists must provide their periodic reports within two weeks after the end of each calendar quarter, establishing a quarterly cadence.
Section 86113 limits the lobbyist's periodic report contents to activity expenses and certain contributions, and does not require disclosure of specific bills/executive actions lobbied.
The lobbyist periodic report requires reporting of activity expenses and contributions, but contains no requirement that the lobbyist disclose compensation received from a client/employer.
The statute does not require lobbyists to disclose contacts; it specifies only reporting activity expenses and certain contributions.
Lobbyist reporting focuses on itemized activity expenses by date/amount/beneficiary and does not require expenditures to be allocated per issue.
No provision in the lobbyist periodic-report requirement compels disclosure of general issues lobbied; it requires only activity expenses and specified contributions.
Because the lobbyist periodic report has no requirement to report lobbying subjects or actions at all, it does not even require general subjects of lobbying.

Activity expenses include gifts and other compensation-like benefits, and the lobbyist must report all activity expenses with date, amount, beneficiary, and description, covering gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging when they benefit covered officials.
The lobbyist periodic report covers 'activity expenses' benefiting officials, not indirect lobbying costs generally (e.g., overhead) unrelated to such beneficiary expenses.
Lobbyists must file an itemized periodic report of all activity expenses with date, amount, beneficiary, description, and payee, even though compensation and bill numbers are not required.
Section 86113 does not require a lobbyist periodic report to disclose the lobbyist's address/phone; those details are required in lobbyist certifications/registrations instead.
The lobbyist periodic report does not require identification of bills/actions discussed or positions; it requires only activity expenses and certain contributions.
Nothing in Section 86113 requires lobbyists to disclose the nature of the principal's business in the lobbyist periodic report.
Section 86113 does not require a lobbyist periodic report to list principals represented or their contact information.
The lobbyist periodic report requirement does not include disclosing the names of principals represented; such information is part of lobbying firm registration, not the lobbyist report.
The lobbyist periodic report provisions do not require reporting specific bill numbers or legislation IDs.
Section 86113 requires reporting activity expenses and certain contributions, but does not require reporting the lobbyist's compensation as a direct lobbying cost.
The lobbyist periodic report requires reporting of activity expenses, but does not require reporting a total expenditures figure toward lobbying.
Lobbyists must file itemized activity-expense reports, but not compensation and bill numbers, satisfying the 'moderate' criterion described in the prompt.

Because activity expenses include expenses benefiting an official or a member of the official's immediate family, and must be reported with beneficiary information, spending on household/immediate family members is reportable.
When activity expenses are reportable, the statute requires the date and amount of each expense and identifies beneficiary and payee, which is itemized rather than only aggregated totals.
